problem_understanding: Choose the maximum saw height so the collected wood is at least the required amount.

steps.claim: For a cut height x, collected wood is sum(max(0, h_i - x)).
steps.justification: Only the part above the saw height is collected.

steps.claim: Collected wood is non-increasing as x increases.
steps.justification: Raising the saw height never increases any tree's contribution.

steps.claim: Binary search the maximum feasible height.
steps.justification: Feasibility is monotonic: if height x is feasible, every lower height is also feasible.

steps.claim: Use 64-bit integers for the accumulated wood total.
steps.justification: The sum of many large heights can exceed 32-bit integer range.

steps.claim: The algorithm runs in O(n log H) time and O(n) space.
steps.justification: Each check scans n trees, and binary search tries O(log H) heights.

algorithm: Binary search cut height between 0 and max height. If collected wood is at least need, record the height and search higher; otherwise search lower.
correctness_argument: By monotonicity, feasible heights form a prefix of the integer range. Binary search maintains the best feasible height seen and returns the maximum feasible value.
final_output_or_verdict: Outputs the maximum feasible cut height.
